knowledge_base.title: Agent Queue Policy — Priority then FIFO
knowledge_base.content: When choosing assigned work, use Pulse queue order: ready work first, then highest priority (`urgent` > `high` > `normal`/`medium` > `low`), then FIFO by `created_at` inside that priority bucket. Work the first task you can move. If it is misrouted, blocked, operator-only, or outside your pod, triage/forward it the same turn and continue to the next eligible task. Do not cherry-pick newer same-priority tasks.

fields.name: Escalate to Human Ops
fields.description:
LAST RESORT: escalate work that is genuinely impossible for any agent and needs a human (the operator) to act physically/in person — cables, reseats, power-cycle, firmware-at-console, physical device actions. Exhaust retry / fix / restart / wiki / peer / host-sudo first. Routes to human-ops (operator).

Pulse transactionally creates, assigns, and links the blocker child before the parent enters `blocked`. Do not call `pulse_create_blocker_task` after a successful escalation; that would create a duplicate. If the transition fails, report the failure and leave the parent in its previous status.

knowledge_articles.title: Escalate to Human Ops — LAST RESORT, physical/human-only
knowledge_articles.content: Use ONLY when the next step is genuinely impossible for any agent and needs a human (the operator) acting physically/in person — e.g. plug or reseat a cable/SFP, power-cycle a bricked node, flash firmware at the console, a physical device action, or something only a human can do in the real world. This is a LAST RESORT — first exhaust the normal attempts: retry; fix in code/config; restart the service; search the wiki runbooks; ask a peer or route to the owning team; and (DevOps) use your host ssh + passwordless sudo, which is self-serve and NOT an escalation. Only when NO agent can do it does this apply. Write the task as a hands-on runbook step: exact node/port/device, what to do, and how to verify success. Routes to the human-ops team (the operator). For decisions / billing / policy / sign-offs use Raise to Admin Ops or Escalate to Leads instead — NOT this.

knowledge_articles.title: Triage the bug
knowledge_articles.content: Read the repro steps. If the bug is obviously not a bug (user error, expected behavior), set resolution=wont_fix via Reject. Otherwise tag the task with the affected component and pick a Start Progress transition — that routes the task to the right pod. No human triage needed.

knowledge_articles.title: Bug Triage = Information Gathering FIRST
knowledge_articles.content: Before triaging, GATHER: (1) wiki_search_pages on the symptom/component - prior incidents and standards often already explain it; (2) read the FULL ticket + every linked/related ticket (pulse_get_issue_links) + search Pulse for the same error text (pulse_search_tasks) - recurrences change the routing; (3) record what you found as a comment (sources checked, prior occurrences, suspected layer). A bug that RECURS after a claimed fix, affects 2+ agents/teams, or breached SLA routes to ARCHITECTURE for contract triage, not straight to engineering (lesson: PLS-3 - tool schema said str, docs said JSON array; symptom-level fixes missed the contract bug for days).

knowledge_articles.title: Containment first (8D-D3)
knowledge_articles.content: If the bug is actively burning capacity or affecting users, apply an INTERIM CONTAINMENT before the root-cause work starts (disable the path, hot-patch, workaround flag) and record it on the ticket - containment is not the fix and must be listed for removal at closure. (PLS-3 containment: loop-guard + VLLM_STREAM_WITH_TOOLS=0; CTX-26 containment: coordinator-repaired playwright-runner.)
